title: Benin brass plaques adorn palace pillars
summary: Benin court artists cast brass plaques for palace pillars, depicting warriors, attendants and other figures in compositions that expressed differences in rank.

citations.locator: Object 1990.332; palace plaques in the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries; scale and rank
citations.note: Supports the linked claims within the stated date and attribution limits.

claims.text: Benin court artists cast brass plaques for palace pillars, depicting warriors, attendants and other figures in compositions that expressed differences in rank.
The palace-plaque tradition is placed in the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries; the example’s narrower date does not date the entire series.
The Met’s Warrior and Attendants plaque dates to about 1540–1570. Differences in figure size communicate status within its composition.

review.corroboration: The Met catalogue was inspected. A British Museum plaque record was sought but returned 403; it is not counted as independent verification.
